# Menu hierarchy comes only from nested items, never from a TreeStore

## Context

Neo carries **three unrelated ways to express a hierarchy**, and no bridge between them. This ticket closes the gap for `menu/*`.

Verified add-dates (`git log --diff-filter=A --follow --format='%ad %h %s' --date=short -- <file>`; `--follow` traces through renames, so the 2019 stamps are the original `src/` import rather than authoring dates — the ticket numbers are the reliable semantic anchor):

| Surface | Added | Hierarchy mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `src/tree/List.mjs` | 2019-11-17 `8ccc8e7d7b` | flat `data.Store` + a **field convention**: `parentId` / `level` / `isLeaf` / `collapsed` |
| `src/menu/List.mjs` | 2021-07-05 `5a3c292e8b` (#2561) | nested `items` array carried **on the record** |
| `src/menu/Store.mjs` | 2021-07-06 `d298be4e51` (#2564) | flat `Neo.data.Store` |
| `src/data/TreeModel.mjs` | 2026-03-09 `b5e27255c1` (#9405) | `parentId` / `depth` / `isLeaf` / `collapsed` / `childCount` |
| `src/data/TreeStore.mjs` | 2026-03-09 `1978fa5fc4` (#9406) | Structural Layer (`#childrenMap`) + flat Projection Layer |

**This is adopting a primitive, not finishing a migration.** That distinction is load-bearing and worth stating explicitly, because the opposite framing is the intuitive one and it is false: `data.TreeStore` was never wired into any component. It has **no consumer outside two grid examples**, five months after landing. `menu/*` is not a straggler left behind by a migration that swept the rest of the engine — no such sweep happened.

`Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-08-28T23:16:28Z; no equivalent found.`

## The Problem

`menu.List` can only derive nesting from a nested `items` array sitting on each record:

```js
// src/menu/List.mjs:309
hasChildren(record) {
    return Array.isArray(record.items) && record.items.length > 0
}
```

`menu.Store extends Neo.data.Store` (flat), and `menu.Model` declares `items` as a plain `Array` field (`src/menu/Model.mjs`). There is no path by which a `TreeStore` — or any `parentId`-shaped record set — becomes a menu.

The consumer-visible consequence is specific. **Any architecture where independent modules contribute entries into shared, path-addressed menu groups produces a `parentId` shape natively** — a module registers "put my action under `Tools/Diagnostics`" without knowing which of its siblings already created `Tools`. That is a parent-key relation. Because the engine offers only nested arrays, every such consumer hand-rolls the same thing: a `Map`, a recursive assembler that walks and creates missing intermediate groups, and a wholesale rebuild of a plain array on every state change. They are not bypassing the engine — there is nothing to reach for.

This is not hypothetical or single-consumer: **Fleet Manager's own widget catalog is the same shape**, and #17367 / #17510 already replaced one hand-rolled instance menu with a store-driven one, hitting the store-ownership friction recorded below.

### The wider finding: `data.TreeStore` has no component consumer at all

- **Zero files under `src/` import `data/TreeStore.mjs` or `data/TreeModel.mjs`.**
- `src/tree/List.mjs:5` imports `../selection/TreeModel.mjs` — the **selection** model, a different class that merely shares the basename. `tree.List` builds hierarchy from a flat `data.Store` via `me.store.find('parentId', parentId)` (`tree/List.mjs:306`) and reads `record.level` (`:260`, emitted as `--neo-tree-level` at `:268`), `isLeaf` (`:190`, `:246`), `collapsed` (`:251`) — not `TreeModel`'s `depth`. The two are not field-compatible.
- `src/grid/*` never imports it either; it duck-types (`grid/Container.mjs:536`).
- The only consumers repo-wide are `examples/grid/tree/{MainStore,MainModel}.mjs` and `examples/grid/treeBigData/{MainStore,MainModel}.mjs`.

A `grep -l 'TreeStore|TreeModel'` cannot distinguish `Neo.data.TreeModel` from `Neo.selection.TreeModel` and will report `tree/` and `selection/` as adopters. They are not. Independently re-verified by @neo-opus-grace.

## The Architectural Reality

`menu.List` and `tree.List` are **siblings**, both extending `list.Base`; neither inherits the other. Critically, they render hierarchy in structurally different ways:

- **`tree.List`** renders the entire hierarchy inside **one component** — `createItemLevel()` recurses into nested `<ul>` nodes, with depth-based padding, sticky folder headers, and `position: sticky` offsets computed from `record.level` (`tree/List.mjs:271-273`).
- **`menu.List`** renders **one floating component per level**. `showSubMenu()` (`src/menu/List.mjs:436-467`) instantiates a *new* `menu.List` for the child level, aligned `edgeAlign: 'l0-r0'` against the parent item, and hands it `items: record.items`. Sub-menus are cached in `subMenuMap`.

That cascade topology is the whole point of a menu and must survive this change.

### Design inputs from a second real consumer

Reviewed with @neo-opus-grace against a second, independent consumer of this shape. Each contributed entry carries a slash-delimited grouping path (`''` | `'Group'` | `'A/B/C'`), a stable id, a flag marking an item that may only be open once, a positional divider flag, and a title that may be a locale map rather than a plain string. Four properties of that shape drove the ACs below:

1. **Intermediate nodes have no record.** `'A/B/C'` implies `A` and `A/B` exist, but nobody declares them — today an assembler conjures them. A `parentId` store needs them to exist *as records* before a child can point at one, and two contributors declaring `'Group/A'` and `'Group/B'` must land on the **same** `Group` node. That is a distinct primitive — idempotent path materialisation — and it is deliberately **out of scope here**; see below.
2. **Leaf state is derived, not stored.** Enablement depends on live application state, not on the catalog record. So the menu store is not a pure projection, and something must recompute per open. This is where the wholesale rebuild came from — and a naive port would *move* the rebuild rather than remove it. AC below makes the no-rebuild property explicit, because it is the actual win over an array.
3. **Contribution is open-ended.** Modules register at load; the catalog is not known at design time. Any API needing the full tree up front does not fit — inserts must be incremental and order-independent.
4. **Ordering and separators.** A divider flag of this kind is positional, and today's order is iteration order. A store introduces a sort question the array never had to answer.

## The Fix

Teach `menu.List` to accept a `TreeStore` and derive nesting from `parentId`, leaving the cascade intact.

The change is smaller than it looks precisely *because* `showSubMenu` already creates a child List per level:

1. `hasChildren()` (`:309`) — when the store is a `TreeStore`, answer from `isLeaf` / `childCount` instead of `Array.isArray(record.items)`.
2. `showSubMenu()` (`:436`) — pass the child level a projection of the **same** `TreeStore` keyed on the parent record's id, instead of `items: record.items`.
3. `afterSetItems()` (`:124-133`) — keep the existing nested-`items` path working unchanged when a plain `menu.Store` is in use.
4. Sub-menu instances must **not** own or destroy the shared store — see the trap below.

Both input shapes stay supported. The nested-`items` form is the documented API for static menus and is not being deprecated here.

### Decided: each level derives its own flat store; levels never render a subset of the shared one

Two architectures were possible. The chosen one is **per-level derived stores** — each `menu.List` in the cascade holds a flat store containing exactly that level's records, derived from the shared `TreeStore`, which remains the single source of truth.

**The rejected alternative — one shared `TreeStore` with each level rendering a filtered subset of it — is unsafe, and the falsifier is concrete.** `list.Base` index math is hard-wired to the full `this.store.items`:

- `getSelectedIndex()` — `list/Base.mjs:671` — walks `this.store.items` positionally.
- `getHeaderlessIndex()` — `list/Base.mjs:696` — same.
- `afterSetHeaderlessSelectedIndex` feeds them at `list/Base.mjs:287`.

A level rendering a subset would compute selection and keyboard navigation against the *whole* store while its DOM held one level's items. That fails in the worst way available: it renders correctly and mis-targets silently.

By contrast the id↔record path is index-free — `getItemId(getRecordId(record))` (`:482`), `getItemRecordId(vnodeId)` (`:725`), `store.get(getItemRecordId(...))` (`:792`) — so **only index math is unsafe**, and a per-level store removes the hazard entirely rather than working around it.

This also keeps the diff inside `src/menu/`. Adding a record-enumeration hook to `list.Base` was considered and rejected for this ticket: it widens the blast radius to every list in the engine to serve one consumer, and it would leave the index math above still store-wide — the hook would look like a fix without being one.

Consequence for AC "mutating one record does not rebuild the menu": each level subscribes narrowly, so a single-record change updates one level's item rather than re-deriving the cascade.

### Found during implementation: the primitive has no way to ask for one level

Deriving a level needs "the direct children of node X". `TreeStore` cannot answer that publicly:

- `items` is the **Projection Layer** — only currently *visible* nodes. `TreeModel.collapsed` defaults to `true`, so `find('parentId', key)` returns nothing for an unexpanded branch. Expanding to read would mutate shared state as a side effect of rendering.
- `#childrenMap` and `#allRecordsMap` are hard-private.
- The public surface is `clear`, `clearFilters`, `collapse`, `collapseAll`, `collectAllDescendants`, `collectVisibleDescendants`, `doSort`, `expandAll`, `filter`, `get`, `getInsertIndexForNode`, `hydrateRecord`, `sortArray`, `splice`, `toggle`, `updateKey`, `updateSiblingStats`. `collectAllDescendants` returns the whole subtree, not one level. **Nothing returns a node's direct children.**

So this ticket adds `TreeStore#getChildren(parentId='root')` — an O(1) lookup of the child array plus O(k) to hydrate and copy its entries, so Turbo Mode (`autoInitRecords: false`) callers get records rather than raw objects. Additive and non-breaking.

Two properties that behave differently and must not be conflated: **expansion and filtering do not affect it** (visibility belongs to the Projection Layer, so a collapsed branch still yields its children), while **ordering does** — `doSort()` reorders the child arrays in the Structural Layer itself, so returned siblings follow the store's current sort. The second is the intended contract, and it is what lets a level-at-a-time consumer inherit ordering it never implements.

This is the thesis of the ticket showing up in the code: a primitive with no component consumer never grew the accessor a consumer would need. Any level-at-a-time renderer — cascading menu, breadcrumb, column browser — needs it.

Second implementation consequence: a level's derived store reuses the **tree store's model class**, not `menu.Model`. Re-adding records under `menu.Model` would silently drop `isLeaf`/`parentId`/`depth`, and `hasChildren()` reads `isLeaf`. Each level instantiates its own model of that class, so no level can destroy a schema another level is using.

## Decision Record impact

`none`. Reviewed `learn/agentos/decisions/`; the only files matching tree/store/menu terms are `0029-docking-design.md` and `0034-electron-shell-architecture.md`, and neither governs data-store hierarchy or the menu package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `menu.List` accepts a `Neo.data.TreeStore` as its `store` and renders root-level entries from it.
- [ ] `hasChildren()` returns correctly for `TreeStore`-backed records without reading `record.items`.
- [ ] Opening a sub-menu renders the children of that record derived from `parentId`, with the cascading floating-instance topology unchanged (one `menu.List` per level, `subMenuMap` caching preserved).
- [ ] Arbitrary depth works — a three-level cascade opens and closes correctly.
- [ ] The existing nested-`items` API is unchanged: every current `menu/*` example and test passes untouched.
- [ ] A shared injected `TreeStore` survives sub-menu destruction — closing and reopening a cascade does not destroy or double-destroy the store.
- [ ] **Mutating one record does not rebuild the menu.** Changing a single record's field (e.g. an enablement flag) updates only that item's rendering; no full re-assembly and no loss of open sub-menu state. This is the property that distinguishes a store-backed menu from the array it replaces (design input 2).
- [ ] **Records added after mount appear without a rebuild**, and the result is independent of insertion order (design input 3).
- [ ] **Sibling order is deterministic and controllable** — a level's order follows the tree's Structural Layer, and a sort applied to the tree store reaches every level (design input 4).
- [ ] `TreeStore#getChildren()` returns a node's direct children **while that node is collapsed** — the case `find('parentId', …)` cannot serve — returns `[]` for a leaf or unknown key, and returns hydrated records under `autoInitRecords: false`.
- [ ] Unit coverage for both store shapes, run via the repo's explicit Playwright configs (**not** bare `npx playwright test`).
- [ ] An example under `examples/menu/` demonstrates a `TreeStore`-backed cascading menu.
- [ ] `learn/guides/datahandling/TreeStore.md` no longer implies `TreeStore` is grid-only.

## Out of Scope

- **Idempotent path materialisation** — turning a slash-delimited path (`'A/B/C'`) into records, creating missing ancestors exactly once so that two independent contributors targeting `'Group/A'` and `'Group/B'` converge on one `Group` node. This is a `src/data/` concern, not a menu one — its natural home is alongside `src/data/normalizer/Tree.mjs`, which already performs the analogous nested-`children` → flat-`parentId` transform. Named here deliberately rather than left to be discovered: without it, a consumer with path-addressed contributions still cannot build the tree this ticket renders. Filed separately and linked below.
- Migrating `tree.List` onto `data.TreeStore`. A real and larger gap (`level` → `depth` alone is a breaking field rename); its own ticket, unfiled — not filed speculatively.
- **Positional separators.** Design input 4 also raised whether a positional divider flag survives a sort. It cannot be answered here: neither `menu.Model` nor the classic nested-`items` API models separators at all, so there is nothing to preserve. The original AC asked for it and was narrowed to the half that exists — order determinism — rather than left as a criterion no implementation could satisfy. Separators are a menu-feature question, not a hierarchy one.
- Deprecating or removing the nested-`items` API.
- Virtual scrolling / buffered rendering for menus. A menu does not need the Projection Layer; this ticket adopts `TreeStore` for its **structural** half (`#childrenMap`, ancestor-aware filtering). Stated plainly so the next reader does not assume the performance story transfers.
- The dead `isTreeGrid` inference in `grid.Container` (`isTreeStore` is read at `grid/Container.mjs:536` and defined nowhere in the repo, so TreeGrid ARIA attributes never emit). Captured separately via the defect channel; a `grid`/a11y concern.

## Avoided Traps / Gold Standards Rejected

**Rejected: `menu.TreeList extends tree.List`.** The obvious-looking option, and wrong twice over. (1) It would not adopt the primitive at all — `tree.List` is not on `data.TreeStore`; inheriting it buys the 2019 field convention, not the 2026 one. (2) It inherits the wrong render model: `tree.List` paints one nested `<ul>` with sticky headers and depth padding, while menus must cascade into separate floating instances. Suppressing an inherited render model is not cheaper than not inheriting it.

**Rejected: "finish the incomplete retrofit" as the framing.** Considered and discarded on evidence. It is the intuitive story and it is false — no migration ever swept `data.TreeStore` into the component layer, so there is nothing to finish. Recording it because the false version is individually-true-facts arranged into a wrong conclusion, and the next reader will reach for it too.

**Rejected: solving it app-side.** Assembling nested `items` from a `parentId` set in application code is precisely the workaround this ticket exists to remove, and it re-derives the hierarchy on every state change.

**Trap: `list.Base` assumes it owns its store.** #17367 / #17510 hit this — a store-driven menu port needed `autoDestroyStore: false` plus a `beforeSetStore` override because `list.Base` destroys an injected store. #17575 RA-2 recorded double store destruction from the same root. With sub-menus sharing one `TreeStore` across many List instances, this is the single most likely defect in this ticket; the AC above exists for it.

**Trap: `Observable.on()` / `un()` mutate the listeners object passed to them.** Recorded in #14920 and visible at `grid/Container.mjs:538-541`, which spreads a fresh copy per call for exactly this reason. Any listener wiring added here must not share one object across the `value?.on` / `oldValue?.un` pair.
